ideas.title: Give Calina real numbers for every Short: a small stats form per episode
ideas.problem: The only way channel results reach Calina is calina_review(project_id, stats) in agents.py: the owner pastes one free-text line into a single input (office.html, 'Weekly review: paste this week's channel stats'). Calina is told to work out what worked from those words plus a list of titles and hooks. There is no per-Short record of how many people stayed past the opening or how long they watched, so she cannot tell a bad hook from a bad ending, and the next batch cannot be told which hooks to repeat. Israa's review is all opinion before upload; nothing measures what the audience did afterwards. YouTube defines the number that matters for a hook: 'Stayed to watch', the percentage of times viewers stayed to watch past the initial seconds of a Short (YouTube Help, reach page).
ideas.gain: Calina's weekly note and every next batch are steered by what viewers did, not by guesses. It also gives the owner the go/no-go memo's numbers without retyping. Measure: after 10 published Shorts, check that the median 'Stayed to watch' of the newest 5 is above that of the first 5; if the form is never filled in, the idea failed. Cost: about 1 extra minute per Short for the owner (YouTube Studio numbers copied by hand).
ideas.test: Free test in practice mode (HQ_SIMULATE=1): (1) normal: 8 episodes with stats, calina_review's task contains the table sorted by Stayed to watch and the note names 2 hooks to repeat and 2 to drop. (2) edge: only 3 episodes have stats, the note says 'too few Shorts to tell' and does not invent a ranking. (3) failure: a stats field left blank or typed as 'n/a', the table shows '-' and the page still saves; nothing crashes and no number is made up. Pass = all three, plus calina_batch's task shows at most 3 best and 3 worst hooks.
ideas.confidence_why: The definition of Stayed to watch rests on YouTube's own help page (A); where Studio shows it is disputed between sources, and the benefit depends on the owner typing the numbers. No benchmark for what a good value is: compare only with our own Shorts.
ideas.risks: Small samples (a handful of Shorts a week) make rankings noisy, hence the 'too few' rule. Views since 31 Mar 2025 count loops, so average percentage viewed can pass 100%: compare it only across our own Shorts, and prefer engaged views as the size of the sample (secondary sources; A source not found). Asking the owner for a new weekly chore costs his 3 hours a week; keep every field optional.
